summary: A toggle for an on/off setting, with its label, description and error beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the track and the accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from naming the inner control. Names the setting, not the action ("Airplane mode", not "Turn on airplane mode").

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when other visible text in the row names the setting.

description.note: Help text under the label: what the setting does, or its consequence.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the switch invalid and sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission (SB-0009).

value.note: Submitted with the form while on; nothing is submitted while off (like a native checkbox).

checked.note: On (true) or off. Not reflected: the attribute is the default that form reset restores.

required.note: Native required: must be on to submit (valueMissing while off). Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed, not focusable, not submitted. A <fieldset disabled> ancestor disables it too without changing this attribute.

size.note: Track 32x20px with a 16px thumb (default) or 24x16px with a 12px thumb (sm). Label typography does not change.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: the switch in the first column; label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Wraps the track and the native input that covers it, so a click anywhere on the track toggles.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">: receives focus, Space and validation; visually transparent over the track.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: Pill-shaped track; its fill shows on (primary) or off (input).

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Round thumb; at the start edge when off, the end edge when on (mirrored in right-to-left).

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root; clicking it toggles.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each user toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary. Not fired when checked is set from code.

change.note: Toggle committed by the user. Re-dispatched from the host because the native change is not composed (NativeControl). Not fired when checked is set from code.

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the track (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with primary and the thumb moves to the end edge; position, not color alone, tells on from off.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt
invalid.note: Track border turns destructive and the error text shows; color is never the only signal.

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or a disabled fieldset ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: FormAssociated + NativeControl: setFormValue(value) only while on, null while off; validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing while off; error -> customError); formResetCallback restores the default checked state (the checked attribute); formStateRestoreCallback restores the saved on/off; disabled directly or by a <fieldset disabled> ancestor is not submitted and cannot be toggled, and re-enabling restores it; a <label for> pointing at the host toggles it.

accessibility.targetSize: Default track is 32x20px; sm is 24x16px (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum 24px wide). The label is part of the clickable row and the gap to neighbors satisfies the 2.5.8 spacing exception; place sm switches with at least 24px between their centers.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px solid ring in switch.focus-ring.color around the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: moves focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the inner control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009). It does not toggle (SB-0101).

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox; the browser exposes aria-checked="true"/"false" from its checked state
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
track and thumb are decorative (aria-hidden); the state is carried by the switch role, never by the label text changing
announcements: the new state (on/off) is announced by the screen reader from the switch role on each toggle
error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off (notifications, dark mode, auto-save)
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label naming the setting

useCases.when: A list of independent settings in a settings form
useCases.use: one sb-switch per setting, each with its own name

useCases.when: The effect of the setting needs explaining
A dense row (table, toolbar-like settings list) needs a smaller control
The setting must be on before the form can be submitted
useCases.use: required, with an error explaining why

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for accepting terms or giving consent
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as a setting that is on or off now; an agreement is a choice recorded with the form
A switch has exactly two states

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch that triggers a one-off action (send, delete)
antiPatterns.why: A switch holds a state; an action is a command

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state ("On" / "Off") or names the action ("Turn on")
antiPatterns.why: The switch role already announces on/off; a changing label makes the name unstable and the state ambiguous
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A pressed/unpressed formatting button (bold, italic) built as a switch
antiPatterns.why: That is a toggle button, announced as pressed, not as on/off

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field and Label parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside
shadcn uses bg-input (neutral-200), below 3:1; changed for WCAG 1.4.11

drift.contract: default track 32x20px, thumb 16px; sm track 24x16px, thumb 12px
drift.realization: shadcn default is 32x18.4px (h-[1.15rem]); rounded to the 4px grid through size.switch.*

drift.contract: off thumb color.background, on thumb color.primary-foreground in every mode
drift.realization: shadcn uses foreground for the off thumb in dark mode; one alias per mode keeps the component layer mode-free

drift.contract: track border in color.destructive plus the error text
drift.realization: shadcn shows aria-invalid only through the surrounding Field
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset (shadcn/Radix reflects data-state)

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern)?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes: APG switch pattern on a native checkbox, label row beside the track, like Checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG switch pattern, label row beside the track. Taken with the recommendation; nobody was available to approve (SB-0011, SB-0101).

openQuestions.question: Which native element carries the switch: <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> or <button role="switch" aria-checked>?
openQuestions.recommendation: The checkbox input with role=switch: native Space, checked state, required/valueMissing and the browser's validation message come for free (SB-0007 native first), and NativeControl already wraps it.
openQuestions.answer: <input type="checkbox" role="switch">. A button would need hand-built checked state, validity and label activation.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch (APG lists it as optional) or submit the form?
openQuestions.recommendation: Enter submits the form, like Checkbox and Input (SB-0009); only Space toggles, as on a native checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: Enter submits the form; Space toggles. Consistent with every other form control in the library (SB-0101).

openQuestions.question: What is submitted while off?
openQuestions.recommendation: Nothing, like a native checkbox; value (default "on") only while on.
openQuestions.answer: Nothing while off; value while on. A separate off-value prop was discarded: servers already read a missing field as off.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: the checked attribute is the default that form reset restores (native defaultChecked), as in Checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: No. checked is a property; the attribute sets the initial and reset state.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, like Checkbox and Input; hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.
openQuestions.answer: Yes. An empty label logs a dev-only warning.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes, and what are their dimensions?
openQuestions.recommendation: The reference's two sizes, default and sm, on the existing size.switch.* semantic tokens: 32x20 and 24x16 track, 16 and 12px thumb, 2px inset.
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20, thumb 16) and sm (24x16, thumb 12). Label typography stays the same in both.

openQuestions.question: How does an invalid switch look?
openQuestions.recommendation: Track border in color.destructive plus the error text and aria-invalid; never color alone.
openQuestions.answer: Destructive track border, error text in the live region, aria-invalid. A destructive track fill was discarded: it reads as on.

openQuestions.question: Which side is the label on?
openQuestions.recommendation: After the switch (end side), like Checkbox; mirrored in right-to-left.
openQuestions.answer: Label after the switch. A label-before/justified settings row is left to the consumer's layout (Item, Field) rather than a prop (YAGNI).

openQuestions.question: Manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver, NVDA) of the on/off announcement once implemented.
openQuestions.recommendation: Run it before the status moves to beta.
